label: 21 April 753 BC
title: Rome founded (traditional date)
text: Romulus founds the city on the Palatine, according to Varro's chronology. The date becomes the Natalis Urbis, still celebrated in Rome every April. Year 1 ab urbe condita.

label: 616–579 BC
title: The Etruscan kings: Tarquinius Priscus
text: The Tarquins drain the Forum (the Cloaca Maxima) and lay out the Circus Maximus. Rome acquires plumbing before it acquires a republic.

label: 509 BC
title: Monarchy overthrown; the Republic founded
text: Tarquinius Superbus is expelled after the outrage against Lucretia. Brutus and Collatinus become the first consuls. SPQR goes live.

label: 494 BC
title: First secession of the plebs
text: The plebeians walk out to the Sacred Mount; the tribunes of the plebs are created. The world's first recorded general strike ends with a new public office.

label: 451–450 BC
title: The Twelve Tables
text: Rome's first written law code is posted in the Forum. Roman law, version 1.0.

label: c. 390 BC
title: Gauls sack Rome
text: Brennus and the Senones defeat the Romans at the Allia and sack the city; only the Capitol holds (geese allegedly involved). "Vae victis."

label: 312 BC
title: Via Appia and Aqua Appia
text: The censor Appius Claudius Caecus builds Rome's first great road and first aqueduct. The infrastructure era begins.

label: 264–241 BC
title: First Punic War
text: Rome builds a navy from scratch (and a captured Carthaginian wreck), wins Sicily, and acquires its first province.

label: 218–201 BC
title: Second Punic War: Hannibal crosses the Alps
text: Elephants, the Trebia, Trasimene, and the catastrophe at Cannae on 2 August 216 BC — tens of thousands of Roman dead in an afternoon. Rome refuses to negotiate.

label: 19 October 202 BC
title: Battle of Zama
text: Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal in North Africa. Carthage is reduced to a client state; Rome becomes the western Mediterranean's only superpower.

label: 146 BC
title: Carthage and Corinth destroyed
text: Carthago delenda est — fulfilled. Greece becomes a province the same year. The Mediterranean is now mare nostrum.

label: 133 BC
title: Tiberius Gracchus killed
text: A tribune is clubbed to death by senators over land reform. Political violence enters the Republic's toolkit and never leaves.

label: 107 BC
title: The Marian reforms
text: Marius opens the legions to the landless poor. Soldiers now owe their loyalty to generals rather than the state. Nothing could possibly go wrong.

label: 88 BC
title: Sulla marches on Rome
text: A Roman army enters the city under arms for the first time. Proscriptions follow in 82 BC. Precedent set.

label: 73–71 BC
title: The Spartacus revolt
text: The Third Servile War: a gladiator's army defeats several Roman forces before Crassus crushes it and lines the Via Appia with 6,000 crosses.

label: 60 BC
title: The First Triumvirate
text: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus form an informal cartel. Caesar takes Gaul (58–50 BC), writes the book on it, and becomes very, very rich.

label: 10 January 49 BC
title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
text: "Alea iacta est." Civil war against Pompey and the Senate: Pharsalus (48 BC), Egypt, Cleopatra, and "veni, vidi, vici" (47 BC).

label: 15 March 44 BC
title: Ides of March: Caesar assassinated
text: The dictator perpetuo is stabbed 23 times at the Theatre of Pompey. The Republic is not, in fact, restored.

label: 2 September 31 BC
title: Battle of Actium
text: Octavian and Agrippa defeat Antony and Cleopatra off western Greece. Egypt is annexed in 30 BC. The last obstacle to one-man rule is removed.

label: 16 January 27 BC
title: Octavian becomes Augustus — Empire v1.0
text: The Senate grants the title Augustus. The Republic continues in name; power is now one man's. The Principate begins.

label: September AD 9
title: Teutoburg Forest
text: Arminius annihilates three legions (XVII, XVIII, XIX) under Varus. Augustus: "Quintili Vare, legiones redde!" Rome's frontier settles on the Rhine.

label: 19 August AD 14
title: Death of Augustus
text: After more than forty years in power he dies at Nola; Tiberius succeeds. The succession problem is now permanent.

label: AD 43
title: Invasion of Britain
text: Claudius adds Britannia (arriving, briefly, with elephants). The province lasts until c. 410.

label: 18 July AD 64
title: Great Fire of Rome
text: Ten of the fourteen districts are damaged; Nero blames the Christians and builds the Domus Aurea. Fiddles had not been invented.

label: AD 69
title: Year of the Four Emperors
text: Galba, Otho, Vitellius, Vespasian. The secret of empire is out: emperors can be made somewhere other than Rome (Tacitus).

label: 24 August AD 79
title: Vesuvius erupts
text: Pompeii and Herculaneum are buried; Pliny the Elder dies investigating. The Colosseum opens the following year with a hundred days of games.

label: AD 117
title: Maximum extent under Trajan
text: Dacia, Arabia, Armenia, Mesopotamia: roughly five million square kilometres. Hadrian immediately trims the edges and builds a wall.

label: AD 122
title: Hadrian's Wall begun
text: 117 kilometres across northern Britain. The Empire discovers the concept of "enough".

label: AD 161–180
title: Marcus Aurelius
text: The philosopher-emperor spends his reign fighting on the Danube and writing the Meditations. The Antonine Plague (165–180) kills millions.

label: AD 212
title: Constitutio Antoniniana
text: Caracalla grants citizenship to nearly every free inhabitant of the Empire. He also raises the taxes that only citizens paid. Coincidence.

label: AD 235–284
title: Crisis of the Third Century
text: Around 26 emperors in fifty years, plague, hyperinflation, and the breakaway Gallic and Palmyrene empires. Aurelian (270–275) stitches it back together.

label: 20 November 284
title: Diocletian and the Tetrarchy
text: Four emperors, price controls, a new tax system, and the Great Persecution. The Dominate replaces the Principate's pretence.

label: 28 October 312
title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
text: Constantine defeats Maxentius under the chi-rho. The Edict of Milan (313) legalises Christianity.

label: 11 May 330
title: Constantinople dedicated
text: Constantine refounds Byzantium as Nova Roma. The centre of gravity moves east for the next 1,123 years.

label: 9 August 378
title: Battle of Adrianople
text: The Goths destroy the Eastern field army and kill the emperor Valens. Ammianus calls it the worst defeat since Cannae.

label: 27 February 380
title: Edict of Thessalonica
text: Theodosius I makes Nicene Christianity the state religion. In 395 the Empire is divided between his sons for the last time.

label: 24 August 410
title: Alaric sacks Rome
text: The first sack in 800 years. Jerome, in Bethlehem: "The city which had taken the whole world was itself taken."

label: 2 June 455
title: Vandals sack Rome
text: Geiseric's fleet sails up the Tiber and loots the city for fourteen days. The word "vandalism" follows — in 1794, but still.

label: 4 September 476
title: End of the Western Empire
text: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus and sends the regalia to Zeno in Constantinople. Root cause: disputed. Postmortem: ongoing, ~1,550 years.

title: Justinian and the reconquest
text: Belisarius retakes Africa (534) and Italy (by 554); the Corpus Iuris Civilis (529–534) and Hagia Sophia (537). The Plague of Justinian (541) undoes much of it.

title: Heraclius
text: Greek replaces Latin in the administration; "Basileus" replaces "Augustus". Persia is defeated (628), then the Arab conquests take Syria and Egypt (636–642).

title: Second Arab siege of Constantinople
text: Leo III and Greek fire hold the Theodosian Walls. Europe's eastern door stays shut for another seven centuries.

label: 25 December 800
title: Charlemagne crowned "Emperor of the Romans"
text: Pope Leo III crowns a Frank in St Peter's. Constantinople is not consulted and is not amused. The Holy Roman Empire follows in 962.

title: The Great Schism
text: Rome and Constantinople excommunicate each other. The mutual anathemas were lifted only in 1965.

label: 26 August 1071
title: Manzikert
text: The Seljuk Turks capture Romanos IV. Anatolia, the Empire's heartland, begins to slip away.

label: 12–13 April 1204
title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
text: Crusaders bound for Egypt sack the largest Christian city instead. The Empire is partitioned; the bronze horses leave for Venice.

label: 25 July 1261
title: Byzantine restoration
text: Michael VIII Palaiologos retakes the capital. The Empire limps on for two more centuries, shrinking to a city and a few outposts.

label: 29 May 1453
title: Fall of Constantinople
text: Mehmed II's cannon breach the Theodosian Walls; Constantine XI dies fighting. 2,206 years after the founding, the Roman state ends. This site exists to check whether that has changed. It has not.

label: 15 August 1461
title: Trebizond surrenders
text: The last Byzantine splinter state falls to Mehmed II. Last known Roman process terminated.

label: 6 August 1806
title: Holy Roman Empire dissolved
text: Francis II abdicates under pressure from Napoleon. The longest-running claimant shuts down after 1,006 years.

label: 15 March 1917
title: The Third Rome logs off
text: Nicholas II abdicates; the last Tsar (from "Caesar") leaves office, and Moscow's Third Rome claim expires with him.

label: 1 November 1922
title: Last Kayser-i Rûm deposed
text: The Ottoman sultanate — whose rulers had styled themselves Caesar of Rome since 1453 — is abolished. Successor claims: 0 active.

label: September 2023
title: The meme
text: A social-media trend reveals that a great many men think about the Roman Empire daily. Monitoring begins. Verdict so far: NO.
